The `FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is rendered in the same JSX tree as the always-visible `HeaderWithBackButton` (the header renders unconditionally above the `{isSelectingBankAccount ? ... : ...}` ternary). Because navigation (the back button) is still on screen while loading, the user already has an escape route, so `FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is the wrong indicator here — it is meant for screens where no navigation is visible and the user would otherwise be trapped.

Use an `ActivityIndicator` inside a centered container instead:

```tsx
{isSelectingBankAccount ? (
    <View style={[styles.flex1, styles.justifyContentCenter, styles.alignItemsCenter]}>
        <ActivityIndicator size="large" />
    </View>
) : (
    <ScrollView ...>
        ...
    </ScrollView>
)}
```

`FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is rendered inside a `ScreenWrapper` without any navigation component (e.g., `HeaderWithBackButton`) in the same return branch. If loading hangs, the user has no escape route. Add `shouldUseGoBackButton` so that an emergency "Go Back" button appears after a timeout.

Suggested fix:
```tsx
<FullScreenLoadingIndicator shouldUseGoBackButton reasonAttributes={{context: 'MultifactorAuthenticationScenarioAuthorizeTransactionPage'}} />
```

`FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is used here without `shouldUseGoBackButton` and no navigation component (e.g., `HeaderWithBackButton`) is visible in this return branch. If loading hangs, the user is trapped with no escape route.

Add `shouldUseGoBackButton` to the `FullScreenLoadingIndicator`:
```tsx
return <FullScreenLoadingIndicator reasonAttributes={reasonAttributes} shouldUseGoBackButton />;
```

`FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is used as an early return when `isLoadingApp` is true. In this code path, no navigation component (e.g., `HeaderWithBackButton`) is rendered, so the user has no way to escape if loading hangs.

Add `shouldUseGoBackButton` to provide an emergency escape route:
```tsx
return <FullScreenLoadingIndicator reasonAttributes={reasonAttributes} shouldUseGoBackButton />;
```

`FullScreenLoadingIndicator` is rendered here without `shouldUseGoBackButton` and no navigation component (e.g., `HeaderWithBackButton`) is visible in the same return statement or conditional branch. If loading hangs, the user has no escape route.

Note: This is a pre-existing issue (only the condition variable name changed from `autoAuthState` to `effectiveAutoAuthState`), but worth addressing. Add `shouldUseGoBackButton` to provide an emergency exit:

```tsx
{(!effectiveAutoAuthState ? shouldStartSignInWithValidateCode : autoAuthStateWithDefault === CONST.AUTO_AUTH_STATE.SIGNING_IN) && <FullScreenLoadingIndicator shouldUseGoBackButton />}
```

**Critical logic bug introduced during rename.** The negation operator `!` before `areOptionsInitialized` was accidentally removed. The original expression was:

```tsx
const showLoadingPlaceholder = !areOptionsInitialized || !didScreenTransitionEnd;
```

But the PR changes it to:

```tsx
const shouldShowLoadingPlaceholder = areOptionsInitialized || !didScreenTransitionEnd;
```

This inverts the meaning: the loading placeholder will now show when options **ARE** initialized (the opposite of the intended behavior), and will almost always be `true` since `areOptionsInitialized || !didScreenTransitionEnd` covers nearly all states. This means the actual content will rarely display.

**Fix:** Restore the `!` negation:

```tsx
const shouldShowLoadingPlaceholder = !areOptionsInitialized || !didScreenTransitionEnd;
```
